judgments.rationale: The edit correctly incorporates the governing statutory exception in paragraph (d)(5) (which provides that nothing in the section allows an individual access to information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding) into the reading of the access requirement under paragraph (d)(1). The resulting summary is accurate, complete, and faithful to the source text.

The proposal introduces an inaccurate requirement by stating that the agency must require every individual, whether accompanied or unaccompanied, to furnish written authorization before access. In fact, paragraph (d)(1) provides that the agency may require a written statement authorizing discussion specifically in the accompanying person's presence.

The unchanged draft C0000 omits the governing statutory limitation set out in paragraph (d)(5), which explicitly restricts access under this section for information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding. Because the unchanged statement lacks this governing exception, it is not an independently complete reading.

source_spans.quote: (d) Access to Records.— Each agency that maintains a system of rec­ords shall—

(1) upon request by any individual to gain access to his record or to any information pertaining to him which is contained in the system, permit him and upon his request, a person of his own choosing to accompany him, to review the record and have a copy made of all or any portion thereof in a form comprehensible to him, except that the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence;
(5) nothing in this section shall allow an individual access to any information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding.
